newsitem.title: UK: ACPC may look at price triggers - delegates.
newsitem.headline: ACPC may look at price triggers - delegates.

text.p: Producing Countries (ACPC) may favour a return to a trigger price mechanism to help regulate future supply to the market, delegates to London coffee talks said on Tuesday.

Few delegates were, however, prepared to discuss details of a draft proposal agreed on Monday by an ACPC technical group, led by Brazil, which is to go forward to a council session of the group scheduled for Wednesday.
A week's deliberations of the larger International Coffee Organization (ICO) continued in London on Tuesday. The ACPC sessions are being held in the margin of that gathering.
Delegates said on Monday that the draft ACPC proposal envisaged retaining export quotas but with an emphasis on flexibility.

In lobby comments on Tuesday, delegates said that while there was less need to restrict supply now, in view of the run-up in world prices, the 14-member group should draw up some plans to cope with future production and market trends.
"We should agree now on what should be done in the future...we can have a system of self-adjusting the floor to the market depending on prices and everything else," said one Latin American delegate.
He said the ACPC could revert to a former supply retention mechanism based on trigger prices that was introduced in 1993.
But ACPC secretary-general Robeiro Oliveria Silva declined to comment when asked about that. Other Asian and African delegates also declined to say anything about the likely action.
Brokerage GNI Ltd noted in a commentary that the ACPC was discussing "ideas on how to make its export quota more flexible".
It said that "the easiest way is to introduce a price ladder similar to the initial retention price ladder introduced at the inception of the organization in 1993.
"That way robusta countries could maintain discipline while arabica producers could ship all of the coffee they don't have". - - London Newsroom +44 171 542 7729
